newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: FRANCE, BELGIUM, LUXEMBOURG TO SPEED RAIL FREIGHT.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE, BELGIUM, LUXEMBOURG TO SPEED RAIL FREIGHT.

text.p: Belgium, France and Luxembourg have struck a deal to create a rail "freight freeway" intended to speed goods traffic between northern Belgium and south-east France, said a statement released on Wednesday.
The route, mapped out in a deal between the three state railway companies, would join Muizen, near the Belgian port of Antwerp, to Sibelin/Venissieux near Lyon via Luxembourg's Bettembourg.

Seven extra daily services, offering journey times cut by one fifth or a quarter, would add two million tonnes to the annual capacity available, said the joint statement by transport ministers from the three countries.
Companies would also offer a "one-stop-shop" to coordinate planning and capacity use.
The "freight freeway" should be in place by the start of next year and will be open to all EU rail operators subject to qualifying criteria of existing EU rules on rail network access.
European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock has fought hard for a system of rapid rail freight routes across the EU to claw back market share for rail and away from road hauliers.

The plan, which Kinnock said got enthusiastic backing from EU transport ministers at their meeting on Tuesday, is intended to raise the 16 kilometre/hour (10 mph) average speed of current rail freight journeys by creating seamless cross-border systems in place of existing national patchworks.
Commission figures for the freight market point to a 150 percent growth in road freight between 1970 and 1995 at the same time as market share for rail-borne goods has halved.
In addition to Wednesday's announced route, plans are afoot for lines linking North Sea ports in Germany and the Netherlands through Austria to Italy.
